Axiom:
A spec lives in two states. **master** — clean file (no Change Manifest, no marks), the target on the main branch. **review-state** — the same file on a working branch during a change: the target text is written IN PLACE (everything else byte-for-byte, so the branch diff reads like a normal PR), with the temporary change manifest loaded by the owning authoring flow at the top and affected lines marked `✚` (new) / `~` (changed). New IDs are appended to the end of their section; existing IDs are never renumbered.
`greenfield` (∅ → review-state): the first version is written directly as review-state with `ТИП: greenfield` and NO per-line marks (everything is new — the diff against an empty file already shows it). `refine` / `pivot` edit an existing master in place WITH marks.
The spec change is a reviewable PR (design-PR). Before the internal critic, finalize semantic bytes (Decision Log compression including merge/delete, ID collision repair, pivot supersession), then obtain the operator's delta-only final hierarchy Approval. The critic loop is necessary but NOT sufficient and owns one global five-result cap across any correction/finalization return; such a return preserves its scratch and next round number. Critic target/write ownership stays specs-only; the separate VCS publication-set may add only mechanically attributed durable authoring outputs (registered research, canonical portal/index files, and the exact session-ignore addition), and any other dirty path halts. After the critic, approve only its actual delta, remove review scaffolding with Critic Rounds last, and pass the final-byte integrity check. Publish exactly the role-validated clean publication-set bytes. External approval names one reviewed commit; merge that same commit with no semantic rewrite afterward. Implementation (scaffold → execute) follows the merged master.
Reconcile has one narrow non-semantic exception: an explicitly classified editorial correction (spelling, formatting, or a mechanical link correction to an already-defined target) may use its frozen task-free target-set plus exact `sdd-check --all` direct receipt. It must change no GOAL, requirement, behaviour, contract, inventory, architecture, dependency, BDD acceptance, risk, or Decision Log meaning. Any such delta is semantic and returns to the authoring + integrated review lifecycle above before scaffold/reopen/execute.
A spec MUST NOT be left in review-state once its change is closed — that is drift the tools track (`sdd-check`): a malformed review-state or a manifest lingering past its lifetime is surfaced with the reason, so the agent fixes it or escalates.
